q: 1. The type of projection in which the surface are equally foreshortened is
explain: In isometric projection all three principal edges/axes of an object are foreshortened equally (by the same isometric ratio, ~0.816), unlike oblique or other projections where foreshortening differs by direction.

q: 2. In comparison to an isometric projection, the appearance of an isometric view is
explain: An isometric projection uses the reduced isometric scale (~0.816 of true length), while an isometric view/drawing is plotted using true (actual) lengths, making the isometric view appear larger than the true isometric projection.

q: 3. In first angle projection method, the relative positions of the object, plane and observers are
options: may be placed in any order
explain: In first angle projection, the sequence is Observer → Object → Plane of Projection, so the object lies between the observer and the plane.

q: 4. A point whose elevation and plan are above XY, is situated in
explain: If both the front view (above XY, meaning in front of VP is reversed logic) and top view lie above the XY line, the point lies in the second dihedral angle (above HP and behind VP).

q: 5. When the picture plane coincide with the object, the perspective of the object will be of its
explain: If the picture plane passes through the object itself, the perspective projection of that portion coincides with the object, so it appears at its actual (same) size.

q: 6. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: A sectional view is created by imagining the object cut by a plane to reveal and clarify hidden internal features that are not visible in a normal view.

q: 7. The nature of surface of sphere is .............
explain: A sphere's surface is curved in two independent directions simultaneously (both meridian and latitude directions), making it a doubly curved surface, unlike a cylinder or cone which are singly curved.

q: 8. In the cabinet projection, an angle at which the projectors meet the plane of projection is .............
explain: Cabinet projection is an oblique projection drawn with receding lines at 30° (some texts use 45°) to reduce distortion, while depth is drawn at half scale; per this reference the receiving angle is taken as 30°.

q: 9. The angle between two perpendicular line is
explain: Perpendicular lines are defined as lines that intersect at a right angle ($90^{\circ}$).

q: 10. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called
explain: The point where the x, y (and z) axes meet is by definition called the origin.

q: 11. Isometric projection, all distances are approximately this percentage of their size
explain: The isometric reduction factor of 0.815 corresponds to roughly 80% of the true size.

q: 12. In perspective drawing, the size of elements depend on .............
explain: In perspective projection, apparent size diminishes with increasing distance from the observer (station point), mimicking how the human eye perceives depth.

q: 13. In case of perspective projection, picture plane is placed
options: out side of eye towards eye
explain: The picture plane is the transparent 'window' situated between the observer's eye and the object being viewed.

q: 14. In orthographic projection which one have all three views same
explain: A cube looks like a square from all principal sides, and a sphere looks like a circle from every direction.

q: 15. If top view of a point is situated 60 mm below the reference line and its front view is 20 mm above the top view, the point lies in .............
explain: A top view below XY indicates the point is in front of VP; a front view further below (only 20mm above the very low top view, i.e., also below XY) indicates it is below HP too — this combination (in front of VP, below HP) places the point in the fourth angle.

q: 16. If the apparent and the true inclinations of a line with HP are equal, the line is .............
explain: The apparent and true inclinations of a line with HP coincide only when the line is parallel to VP, since there is then no distortion of the angle in the front view.

q: 17. The point at which the line intersects the VP, extended if necessary, is known as .............
explain: The point where a line (extended if necessary) meets the Vertical Plane is called the Vertical Trace (VT) of the line.

q: 18. Isometric projection of a sphere is a circle having a diameter
explain: Because a sphere looks the same from every direction, its isometric projection is a true circle equal to the sphere's actual diameter.

q: 19. The other name of axonometric projection is
explain: Axonometric projection represents 3D objects on a single (one) plane of projection.

q: 20. As the distance of an object from the observer increases, its size in the perspective view .............
explain: In perspective projection, objects farther from the observer subtend a smaller visual angle, so their apparent size in the perspective view decreases with increasing distance, matching real-world visual perception.

q: 21. The imaginary vertical plane passing through the observer's eye is called .............
explain: The central plane is the imaginary vertical plane passing through the observer's eye (station point) and perpendicular to the picture plane, used as a reference in perspective construction.

q: 22. In one plane drawing, which one does not falls under
explain: Standard orthographic projection usually involves multiple planes (multi-view); axonometric, oblique, and dimetric are single-plane pictorials.

q: 23. Axonometric projection is a special types of
explain: Axonometric is a sub-type of orthographic projection because the projectors are perpendicular to the plane.

q: 24. A right circular cone when cut by a plane parallel to its generator, the curve obtained is a .............
explain: When a cutting plane is parallel to one generator (slant side) of a right circular cone, the section produced is a parabola, per the standard classification of conic sections.

q: 25. The receding lines in an isometric projection are drawn
explain: The receding lines in an isometric drawing that represent depth are drawn parallel to the corresponding isometric axis.

q: 26. The polyhedra having a plane figure for its base and equal number of isosceles triangular faces meeting at a point is called a .............
explain: A pyramid has a single base and faces that taper to a single point called the apex.

q: 27. Orthographic projection means:
explain: Orthographic projection uses projectors perpendicular to the projection plane, forming right angles, consistent with a right-angled triangle relationship.

q: 28. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of product including civil construction, are known as
explain: Working drawings provide all necessary dimensions and details required to actually manufacture or build the project.

q: 29. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and plane of projection are
explain: The word 'ortho' means right angle; the projectors (lines of sight) must be perpendicular to the projection plane.

q: 30. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called
explain: Perspective drawing is the only projection method that accurately replicates the human visual experience.

q: 31. Plan, elevation and sections are
explain: Plans, elevations and sections are all views obtained by orthographic (parallel, perpendicular) projection.

q: 32. In the first angle projection
options: The plan is above the front view
The plan is directly below the front view
The plan is as in the third angle projection
explain: In first angle projection the plan (top view) is placed below the front view, opposite to the third angle convention.

q: 33. In the cavalier projection, an angle at which the projectors meet the plane of projection is .............
explain: Cavalier projection is characterized by receding lines drawn to full (true) scale with projectors typically inclined at 45° in most texts, but per this reference the projector angle is taken as 63°26'.

q: 34. Horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP) are always
explain: In the standard system of orthographic projection, HP and VP are set up perpendicular to each other, intersecting along the reference line (XY line).

q: 35. The projection obtained on a plane when the projectors converge to a point is known as
explain: Perspective projection uses projectors that converge at a single station point (the observer's eye), unlike parallel-projector methods.

q: 36. Among the following solids, a regular polyhedron is .............
explain: A regular polyhedron has all faces as identical regular polygons meeting in the same way at each vertex; among the given options, only the cube (all faces equal squares) satisfies this, while a sphere is not a polyhedron at all.

q: 37. The projection in which the length, breadth and height of an object is shown in one view is Known as :
explain: Isometric projection is a type of pictorial projection that shows all three dimensions in a single view at specific angles.

q: 38. Isometric projection of a sphere is a circle having a diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'less than that of sphere' is marked correct here; this corresponds to isometric projection drawn using the true (reduced) isometric scale (~0.816), giving a projected circle smaller than the sphere's actual diameter.

q: 39. In 1st angle projection the right side view must be drawn on .... side of the FV:
explain: In first angle projection each view is placed on the side opposite to the direction it is viewed from, so the right side view appears to the left of the front view.

q: 40. Perspective drawing are mostly used in drawing:
options: elevation of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
side view of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
explain: As given by the answer key, none of the specific listed options is the standard answer; perspective drawings are generally used for realistic presentation views rather than technical plans/elevations.

q: 41. A tetrahedron is resting on its face on the HP with a side perpendicular to the VP. Its front view will be .............
explain: With a tetrahedron resting on a triangular face on HP and one edge perpendicular to VP, the front view (projected along the direction perpendicular to VP) appears as an isosceles triangle due to the way the base edge foreshortens.

q: 42. If both front and top views of a plane are straight lines the true shape will lie on .............
explain: When both principal views collapse to straight lines, the plane is perpendicular to both HP and VP, meaning it is parallel to the profile plane; conventionally this would place the true shape on the profile plane specifically, but per this reference, option (d) is marked as the general answer.

q: 43. If a circular plane is inclined at 30° with the HP and 60° with the VP its side view will be .............
explain: Since the given inclinations (30° to HP and 60° to VP) sum to 90°, the plane is perpendicular to the profile plane, so its side view is seen edge-on as a straight line.

q: 44. The projectors in isometric view are .............
explain: Isometric projection is a form of orthographic (parallel) projection, so its projectors remain parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 45. The way of illustrating three dimensional objects in a two dimensional drawing is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'perspective' is marked correct here; more broadly, several methods (axonometric, perspective, oblique) are used to represent 3D objects in 2D, but the given key highlights perspective as the intended answer for this item.

q: 46. When a pendulum oscillates, name the locus of a point moving along its string at a constant speed .............
explain: A point moving at constant speed along a pendulum's string, whose length itself changes (winds/unwinds) uniformly, traces a spiral curve.

q: 47. A cone is cut by a section plane parallel to the profile plane. Its true shape of section is seen in .............
explain: Since the cutting plane is parallel to the profile plane, the true shape of the resulting section is revealed in the side (profile) view, which is taken looking along a direction parallel to that plane.

q: 48. If a polyhedron is cut by any section plane, the true shape of section is a closed figure made up of .............
explain: Since a polyhedron's faces are all flat planar surfaces, any section cut through it produces a closed figure bounded entirely by straight line segments (where the cutting plane meets each flat face).

q: 49. The drawings in which the receding lines are drawn to half the scale are called .............
explain: Cabinet projection is the oblique projection type in which receding lines are drawn at half their true length (half scale), reducing the distortion seen in full-scale cavalier projection.

q: 50. A perspective drawing of a high rise tower is prepared using the number of vanishing points as .............
explain: For tall structures like a high-rise tower, three-point perspective is used, adding a third vanishing point (above or below) to correctly depict the vertical convergence of lines when viewed from a strongly elevated or low angle.

q: 51. In oblique projections, the receding lines meet the plane of projection at an angle .............
explain: By definition, oblique projection is characterized by projectors that strike the plane of projection at an angle other than 90°, i.e., at an angle less than 90°.

q: 52. When a right circular cone is cut which meets its axis at an angle greater than the semi-apex angle, the curve obtained is .............
explain: When the cutting plane's angle with the axis exceeds the semi-apex angle of the cone (and it does not pass through the apex), the section obtained is a closed curve — an ellipse.

q: 53. When a right circular cone is cut which meets its axis at an angle less than the semi-apex angle, the curve obtained is .............
explain: When the cutting plane's angle with the axis is less than the cone's semi-apex angle, the plane intersects both nappes of the cone, producing an open hyperbolic section.
